newsitem.title: USA: Rubin - disputes should not hurt U.S./China ties.
newsitem.headline: Rubin - disputes should not hurt U.S./China ties.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin Monday said that it would be a mistake to let individual disagreements affect overall U.S.-China relations.

In a statement issued at the beginning of a two-day session between U.S. and Chinese officials, Rubin said that by working together and developing a deeper understanding of differing economic views, the two countries can move toward reconciling their differences.
"The key is not to let individual disagreements affect the overall relationship and to work constructively to resolve the disagreements whenever possible," Rubin said.
Rubin met with a Chinese delegation led by Finance Minister Liu Zhongli under the umbrella of the U.S.-China Joint Economic Commission.
In his statement he said he hoped to move forward in a pragmatic way in addressing various issues.

"As examples, for China, I believe that the process will improve prospects for WTO (World Trade Organization) accession -- which the U.S. supports on commercially meaningful terms. For the United States, a key issue is the magnitude of our bilateral trade deficit, and the policies that affected," he said.
In discussing the agenda for the next two days, Rubin said they would examine recent economic performance, approaches to macroeconomic management, structural issues and bilateral trade balances.
He said the U.S. delegation was eager to "discuss with China its next steps in introducing market-oriented forces into its economy."
In addition, he said the delegations will "delve into" financial market reform and supervision and the "ramifications" of the passage by China of a central bank and commercial bank law last year.
